entries.title: Guardian angels
entries.quote: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.
entries.line: Jesus warns against despising children, grounding it in the reality that their angels continually behold the Father's face — the clearest text for individual angelic guardianship.

entries.title: Entertaining angels unawares
entries.quote: Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.
entries.line: The writer of Hebrews urges hospitality by recalling Abraham and Lot — both hosted angels without recognizing them at first (GEN 18–19).

entries.title: Angels charged to keep you
entries.quote: For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.
entries.line: The psalmist promises divine protection through angelic guardianship — a verse the devil himself quotes back at Jesus in the wilderness (MAT 4:6; LUK 4:10–11).

entries.title: Like angels in the resurrection
entries.quote: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
entries.line: Jesus answers the Sadducees: the resurrected state transcends marriage, resembling the angelic mode of existence — neither marrying nor dying.

entries.title: We will judge angels
entries.quote: Don’t you know that we will judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?
entries.line: Paul rebukes the Corinthians for taking disputes to pagan courts, reminding them that believers will participate in judging angels — a staggering dignity.

entries.title: Even an angel preaching another gospel
entries.quote: But even though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you any “good news” other than that which we preached to you, let him be cursed.
entries.line: Paul anchors gospel authority above any messenger — even an angel from heaven. The message, not the messenger, is the test.

entries.title: Serving spirits
entries.quote: Aren’t they all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?
entries.line: The writer's summary of what angels are for: sent out to serve those who will inherit salvation, not to be served.

entries.title: The angels worship the Son
entries.quote: Let all the angels of God worship him.
entries.line: In the argument that the Son is greater than the angels, the writer has all of them worship him.

entries.title: Created through him
entries.quote: For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him.
entries.line: Thrones, dominions, principalities, powers — the invisible order is created, and created through Christ and for him. This is the verse behind “things visible and invisible”.

entries.title: Not to be worshiped
entries.quote: Let no one rob you of your prize by self-abasement and worshiping of the angels, dwelling in the things which he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
entries.line: Paul warns Colossae against a religion of angel-worship and visions; the angels are not the prize.

entries.title: A fellow servant
entries.quote: You must not do that! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers, the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.
entries.line: John falls before the angel who showed him the visions and is stopped at once: the angel is a fellow servant, and worship belongs to God.

entries.title: Made subject to him
entries.quote: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers being made subject to him.
entries.line: Angels, authorities, and powers are placed under the risen Christ at God's right hand.

entries.title: Not against flesh and blood
entries.quote: For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world’s rulers of the darkness of this age, and against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
entries.line: Paul names the real opposition — principalities, powers, rulers of this darkness, spiritual forces in the heavenly places — and answers it with armor, not fascination.

entries.title: The demons also believe
entries.quote: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.
entries.line: James's test of faith: belief that God is one is something even the demons have, and it makes them shudder, not righteous.

entries.title: Doctrines of demons
entries.quote: But the Spirit says expressly that in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,
entries.line: Paul expects falling away in later times, and traces some false teaching to seducing spirits rather than to error alone.

entries.title: Sacrifice to demons
entries.quote: But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I don’t desire that you would have fellowship with demons.
entries.line: Paul says of pagan sacrifice what Deuteronomy said of Israel's apostasy: it is offered to demons, and fellowship at that table is real.

entries.title: Test the spirits
entries.quote: Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
entries.line: Not every spirit is to be believed; John gives the church a duty to test them, because false prophets have gone out.

entries.title: Mighty in strength, obeying his word
entries.quote: Praise Yahweh, you angels of his, who are mighty in strength, who fulfill his word, obeying the voice of his word.
entries.line: The psalm calls on the angels to praise, and describes them by their obedience: they fulfill his word and listen for his voice.

entries.title: Encamps around
entries.quote: Yahweh’s angel encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
entries.line: David's psalm of deliverance: Yahweh's angel camps around those who fear him — protection as a settled presence, not a single rescue.

entries.title: Twelve legions
entries.quote: Or do you think that I couldn’t ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?
entries.line: At his arrest Jesus says he could ask for more than twelve legions of angels — the Roman word for thousands — and does not.

entries.title: Triumph over the powers
entries.quote: Having stripped the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
entries.line: Paul depicts Christ's cross as a public triumph over principalities and powers; translations differ on whether the verb is rendered ‘disarmed’ or ‘stripped.’

entries.title: Destroying the power of death
entries.quote: that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
entries.line: The incarnation and death of Jesus targeted the root of demonic subjugation: destroying the devil who wielded the power of death, delivering those held lifelong in fear.

entries.title: God in the divine assembly
entries.quote: God presides in the great assembly. He judges among the gods.
entries.line: On a divine-council reading, Psalm 82 depicts God judging other elohim; other interpreters understand the figures as human rulers or judges.
